Using a password manager is one of the simplest and most effective steps you can take to protect your online accounts. Most people have dozens or even hundreds of accounts, and remembering a unique, strong password for each one is simply not realistic. As a result, many people reuse the same password across multiple sites, which is a serious security risk.

If one website suffers a data breach, attackers will often try the leaked credentials on other popular services. This technique, known as credential stuffing, is highly effective against reused passwords. A password manager solves this problem by generating a long, random password for every account and storing it securely.

You only need to remember a single strong master password. The manager then fills in your credentials automatically, which also helps protect against phishing, since it will not autofill on a fake website. Many managers also alert you to weak or compromised passwords and support two-factor authentication codes.

While no tool is perfect, the security benefits far outweigh the risks. Choose a reputable provider, enable two-factor authentication, and start migrating your accounts today.
